cards.power: Play to view opponent's hand. If caught, discard your entire deck.
cards.lore: The first thing in any system that matters. Everything awful that follows begins with their report.
cards.gradeReason: Big risk/reward, but the role is more spy than performance — needs a beat to embody.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: watercolor sci-fi splatter. Subject: needle-thin scout ship with cockpit eye. Mood: surveillance dread.

cards.power: Bypass all electronic traps. The ship literally out-vibes the radar.
cards.lore: Piloted by a "young" Vael—which means it's only been alive for a few centuries.
cards.gradeReason: Out-vibes the radar slaps, but the rest is mood — almost-knockout.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: prismatic watercolor. Subject: butterfly-winged starship. Mood: silent, opalescent stealth.

cards.power: Deal 2 damage to a neutral target just to establish dominance.
cards.lore: Ossian scouts interpret "survey the system" as "establish the Hegemony's claim by shooting the scenery."
cards.gradeReason: Shooting the scenery to establish dominance — player knows exactly how to play it.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: punk watercolor. Subject: snarling-jaw warship. Mood: belligerent territorial swagger.

cards.power: Move an objective instantly. The ship takes 1 damage per transit until it vaporizes.
cards.lore: The galaxy's nervous system, crewed by fatalists hauling diplomatic secrets worth more than their lives.
cards.gradeReason: Vaporizing courier is dramatic; the lore explains rather than invites the fatalism.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: streaked watercolor. Subject: dart-fast courier vessel. Mood: terminal-velocity resignation.

cards.power: Generate 3 Resource tokens. Extrapolate opponent's strategy based on their discards.
cards.lore: The circulatory system of a dying galaxy. If they stop arriving, the sector is already dead.

cards.artworkPrompt: Style: industrial watercolor. Subject: cargo-laden freighter hulk. Mood: exhausted commerce.

cards.power: Block one attack against a Hauler. Farm mid-level management stress.

cards.artworkPrompt: Style: sharp watercolor. Subject: agile escort fighter. Mood: bureaucratic burnout-in-uniform.

cards.power: Double attack power, half defense. Cannot retreat. Ever.

cards.gradeReason: Cannot retreat. Ever. is a posture, a voice, a whole table dynamic.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: fire-streaked watercolor. Subject: stub-nosed warship. Mood: kamikaze conviction.

cards.power: Cancel opponent's attack by burying them in legal injunctions and electronic warfare.

cards.artworkPrompt: Style: corporate-noir watercolor. Subject: dollar-bristling cruiser. Mood: predatory litigation.

cards.power: Instantly claim a system. Opponent must spend 5 turns complaining to the galactic UN.

cards.artworkPrompt: Style: imperial watercolor. Subject: vortex-belching capital warship. Mood: ostentatious dominance.

cards.power: Eradicate target system. Costs the industrial output of your entire hand.

cards.artworkPrompt: Style: gothic watercolor. Subject: cathedral-spired dreadnought. Mood: industrial massacre.

cards.power: Relocate your home base. Becomes politically immune to standard attacks.
cards.lore: A sovereign community in transit. The ultimate geopolitical headache for every border guard.
cards.gradeReason: Strong concept, but role is bureaucratic-shrug rather than knockout embodiment.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: globe-print watercolor. Subject: city-mantled ark-world. Mood: nomadic sovereignty.

cards.power: Execute an action completely off the record. If accused, deny everything.

cards.power: Introduce a new rule to the game. Neither player understands how it works yet.

cards.power: Steal an artifact from opponent's discard pile. Claim it was yours all along.

cards.power: Sabotage an opponent's play, completely off the record.

cards.artworkPrompt: Style: shadow-cabinet watercolor. Subject: badger sniper at podium-rally. Mood: covert reset.

cards.power: Force a delivery through an opponent's defense. Survive on sheer luck.

cards.power: Draw blindly from the deck. You might win the game, you might instantly die.

verdict: Kosmik Kollektive II is FrizzleBob's tightest faction sandbox so far — the punchlines are load-bearing, not decoration. Knockout lines like 'spend 5 turns complaining to the galactic UN', 'Every negotiation is a hostage situation', and the closing 30K-year note give the deck a real spine. Weak spot: the Endgame and a few Weird Shit cards lean lore-only and lose the performance prompt that makes the rest of the deck sing. Table-ready: YES.
blurb: A 56-card sci-fi faction sandbox for players who want to embody a hegemony, a heresy, or a hauler captain — performative space opera that turns every play into a hostage negotiation, a UN complaint, or a cosmic existential shrug.

notes: All card text appears baked into the page images (decorative typewriter/Bangers-style headers, Special Elite-style body), so text is rasterized but consistently legible at print size. RAF dice boxes not present on this deck. Structural pattern: 14 thematic half-suites (Pests & Postmen / Grunt Workers / Imperial Hammers / Blood & Iron / Scum & Weirdness / Meddling & Stealing / Running & Praying / Holes in the Map / Things in the Dark / Basic Cheats / Dangerous Cheats / Puppet Masters / Wildcards / Endgame), 4 cards each = 56 cards. Faction names (Dreshkai, Ossian, Vael, Sorn, Mycel, Prior, Unbound) recur as voice-anchors, building a usable shared world across the deck. Closing card (Thirty-Thousand-Year Note) is a deliberate mic-drop and works as such. Re-analyzed from rendered PNG images after prior interrupted run produced a partial JSON with OCR-style typos (Relocats / Eaecute / immuns).

marketingText:
Kayfabizarro: KOSMIK KOLLEKTIVE (LONG DARK II) – A Galaxy of Factions That Will Outlast You (Free Cut & Play Comic Card Game)

Pick a hegemony, pick a heresy, or pick the hauler captain with the falsified transponder. The galaxy will not tell you which one was the mistake.

Seven peoples share this dark and not one of them shares a goal. The Dreshkai swing imperial hammers, the Prior preach to anyone still receiving, the Mycel spread where nobody invited them, and the Vael keep a ledger so old the debt has outlived the borrower. Fourteen thematic half-suites run from Grunt Workers and Imperial Hammers to Holes in the Map and Things in the Dark, and every play you make lands as one of three honest things: a hostage negotiation, a formal complaint nobody will ever read, or a shrug that takes a thousand years to finish.

This is Social Story Wrestling at the scale of deep time. You take a faction, you perform its angle with a straight face, and the table rules whether the bit holds or gets swallowed by the quiet between stars. Fifty-six cut-and-play cards, seven recurring cultures, and a shared world that assembles itself across the deck while you argue over who owns the wreckage.

WHAT'S INSIDE?
- The Long Dark II Core Deck: 56+ High-Res "Print, Cut & Play" Cards, featuring FIRST CONTACT (the instant two civilizations meet and immediately disagree about who flinched), THE VAEL (ancient creditors whose patience is just leverage wearing a longer clock), and THE THIRTY-THOUSAND-YEAR NOTE (the closing promissory mic-drop that bills an empire long after the empire is dust).
- The Freestyle Rules: the complete Anti-Rulebook. No complicated math, no tech trees, no orbital spreadsheets, just storytelling, dice-driven chaos, and the standing law that every card can claim anything until the table calls the bluff.
- The Faction Engine: seven playable cultures, the Dreshkai, the Ossian, the Vael, the Sorn, the Mycel, the Prior, and the Unbound, each one a different way to want the wrong thing across a galaxy that has stopped answering hails.

THE "LIVING DECK" PASS (Free Updates)
Grab this and you are not buying a sealed file. Long Dark II is the next jump in the same voyage, and the signals that follow reach you as free updates. Same dark, same factions, more wreckage to fight over.

WHY "PAY WHAT YOU WANT"?
I draw these because a galaxy this convinced of its own importance deserves a table full of people willing to heckle it back, and improv crews deserve stranger toys than the market bothers to print. Broke? Enter "0" and take it. Print it, cut it, lose an evening among unfriendly stars. Want to support the craft? Every dollar goes straight into the time I spend drawing the next deck. Free to use, share, and adapt under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Share freely, attribute honestly, never resell.

Choose your reality. Become an Epistemic Outlaw.
"Every empire signs the thirty-thousand-year note and calls it permanence. Play your part long enough to watch the ink fade."
Stay fluffy. — Uncle FrizzleBob
